hints: Look at the type of bond around each carbon, single, double or triple, as this tells you how many sigma and pi bonds are present.
Notice the two carbons joined by the triple bond each have only two sigma-bond regions, while the $\text{CH}_3$ carbon has four single bonds.
Recall that two sigma regions means sp, three means $\text{sp}^2$ and four means $\text{sp}^3$, then check which types actually appear in $\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$.
walkthrough:
**Draw out propyne clearly**

Great start, let us make the structure friendly. Propyne is $\text{H-C}\equiv\text{C-CH}_3$.

So we have three carbons in a row: C1 with one H, C2 in the middle, C3 with three Hs.

**Link bonds to hybridisation**

Here is the key rule to remember. Count sigma-bond regions around each carbon.

$$2 \text{ sigma regions} = sp, \quad 3 \text{ sigma regions} = sp^2, \quad 4 \text{ sigma regions} = sp^3$$

A triple bond is one sigma plus two pi, a double bond is one sigma plus one pi, a single bond is one sigma.

**Apply to the two triple-bond carbons**

Look at the left $\text{H-C}\equiv$ carbon. It has one $\text{C-H}$ sigma plus one $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ sigma. That is 2 sigma regions.

The middle $\equiv\text{C-}$ carbon has one $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ sigma plus one $\text{C-C}$ sigma. That is also 2 sigma regions.

$$2 \text{ sigma regions} \rightarrow sp \text{ hybridisation}$$

**Apply to the methyl carbon**

Now look at the right $-\text{CH}_3$ carbon. It has four single bonds, three to H and one to C. That is 4 sigma regions and no pi bonds.

$$4 \text{ sigma regions} \rightarrow sp^3 \text{ hybridisation}$$

So we see only sp and $\text{sp}^3$, with no $\text{sp}^2$ carbon present.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests all three types are present. There is no $\text{C=C}$ double bond in propyne, so no carbon has 3 sigma regions and no $\text{sp}^2$ hybridisation occurs.
options.B: Correct. The two $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ carbons each have 2 sigma domains so are sp hybridised, and the $\text{CH}_3$ carbon has 4 sigma bonds so is $\text{sp}^3$ hybridised.
options.C: Incorrect. The $\text{sp}^3$ part is right for the methyl carbon, but $\text{sp}^2$ is for alkenes with a double bond. The triple bond carbons need sp, not $\text{sp}^2$.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{sp}^2$ only would fit an alkene like propene. Propyne is an alkyne with a triple bond (sp) plus a saturated methyl group ($\text{sp}^3$).
